reasons.reason: The Yarkovsky effect comes from a body absorbing heat unevenly and releasing it again, and that same cycle of uneven internal heating is what warms moons that are flexed by their planets.
The Yarkovsky effect comes from a small body absorbing sunlight and re-radiating it as heat in a different direction, which gives a tiny steady push that slowly shifts an asteroid's orbit.
Induced ovulation means the female releases eggs only after mating sets it off, so the distinguishing feature is the copulatory trigger replacing the internal hormonal cycle that birds run on.
Many squamates breed on a tight annual cycle tied to the seasons, so their oocytes are released on that calendar whether or not mating has happened, which sets them apart from birds.
The Eddington limit is a threshold set by an object's mass, and for collapsed objects it marks how massive something has to be before it ends up as a black hole instead of a neutron star.
The Eddington limit is the luminosity at which outward radiation pressure on infalling gas equals the inward pull of gravity, so it describes that balance point for accreting objects.

The acceleration showed up as distant supernovae looking fainter than expected, and the explanation that fits is a smooth component with negative pressure filling space, which is what dark energy means.

Baryon acoustic oscillations are the main measurement tying the expansion history together, and the pattern they leave in galaxy clustering is what reveals the expansion speeding up over the last few billion years.
Europa's ice shell has bands where surface material seems to vanish downward, which points to subduction, so geologists classify its faults by measuring how steeply the ice plunges at those zones.
Fault classification anywhere rests on how the two sides moved, sideways or up and down, and Europa's cracks and ridges show offset features that let geologists read exactly that displacement.
Spacecraft go through repeated temperature swings, and each cycle can push a dissolved drug out of solution, so ampicillin crystallizes and precipitates and loses its usable potency over time.
The beta-lactam ring is notoriously sensitive to water, and humidity inside crewed modules keeps rising and falling, so hydrolysis opening that ring is the most direct route to degradation.
For a non-rotating mass, the Schwarzschild radius is the distance from the center at which escape velocity reaches light speed, and that boundary is exactly the event horizon.
The Schwarzschild radius is the size scale of the collapsed matter at the center, so it describes how wide the singularity region is when measured straight across from one side to the other.
Near a black hole, gravity on the nearer end of an object is far stronger than on the far end, so the body gets stretched out into a long thin strand like a noodle.
When a moon or comet wanders too close to a planet, tidal forces draw it out into long strands that then spread around the planet, and those stretched strands become a ring system.

The Permian-Triassic extinction cleared out most competing vertebrates, and temnospondyls appear in many new forms across early Triassic rocks, which fits a fast diversification into the emptied niches.

Many Triassic temnospondyls had flattened heads, sprawling limbs and aquatic habits that look strikingly like giant salamanders, which suggests the same body plan evolved independently in both lineages.
The lumped model treats the solid as cooling with one simple profile, and that only works if the temperature gradient inside stays linear and steady the whole time the body cools.
The lumped model treats the whole body as one temperature, which only holds when conduction inside is much faster than convection at the surface, meaning a small Biot number.
Milankovitch cycles repeat over tens of thousands of years, matching how the shape of Earth's orbit and the tilt of its axis slowly change the sunlight different latitudes receive.

Milankovitch cycles are long climate swings, and large eruptions inject sulfate aerosols that cool the planet, so clusters of eruptions over long spans set up the repeating cold periods seen in the record.
Heat loss in a conductor is the power dissipated in its resistance, and writing it as current squared times resistance shows that doubling the current quadruples the loss, which drives line design.

Over interstellar distances power would be sent as beamed photons rather than through wires, and the same current and resistance relation gives the losses that set how efficient that beaming system is.

The microwave background arrives from every direction, and active galactic nuclei are spread across the whole sky and emit strongly at radio and microwave wavelengths, so together they account for it.
The microwave background is the cooled thermal radiation released when the early universe became transparent, so it is leftover light from the hot dense beginning the Big Bang describes.

Supernova remnants are scattered through every galaxy and radiate for thousands of years, so their combined emission, shifted over cosmic distances, forms a uniform background glow in every direction.
The background radiation is the faint thermal glow from the hot early universe, stretched by expansion into microwaves, so it is the remnant heat of the Big Bang.
Dust grains absorb ultraviolet light very strongly, so measuring how ultraviolet starlight gets blocked and dimmed is the most sensitive way to detect cold dust clouds between the stars.
Cold dust sits at only tens of kelvin, and a body that cold emits its thermal radiation at long wavelengths, so the far-infrared is where the dust itself glows.
A standard candle needs a known true brightness, and Type Ia explosions reach nearly the same peak luminosity because the white dwarfs blow up at about the same mass.
These explosions come from white dwarfs reaching a set mass limit, so their brightness depends on that progenitor mass, and because the mass is fixed the output becomes predictable.
Earth has a large iron-nickel core and its interior is squeezed hard by its own gravity, which gives it the highest average density of any planet orbiting the Sun.
Mars is a rocky planet whose iron-rich surface gives it its red color, and all that iron through its crust packs more mass into each unit of volume than the others listed.
From the Moon's distance, even a huge building or wall subtends an angle far smaller than the eye can separate, so it blurs into its surroundings however large it seems on the ground.
Light reflected from the surface has to pass through the whole atmosphere on its way out, and scattering there washes out fine detail, so narrow structures get lost in the haze.
Zodiacal light is a faint glow that shows up along the band where the Moon travels, and the Moon's reflected sunlight lingers in the sky near that path even when it sits below the horizon.
Zodiacal light is a faint cone along the ecliptic, the plane where dust from comets and asteroids collects, so it is sunlight scattered back to us off that interplanetary dust.
Hayashi worked out that young protostars are fully convective while they shrink, which forces them down a nearly vertical line on the HR diagram before they reach the main sequence.
A track in stellar evolution follows a star's late changes in brightness, and the most dramatic change is the explosion itself, so the Hayashi track traces how a supernova's light rises and fades.
The Kármán line sits at roughly the height where air becomes too thin for wings to give lift, so above it a craft has to fly by orbital speed, which marks where space begins.

The Kármán line marks where the atmosphere changes character, and the sharpest change in the lower atmosphere is where temperature stops falling with height, which is the troposphere-stratosphere boundary.
Hepcidin is the hormone that controls how much iron the gut takes in, and when the body has surplus iron in orbit, raising hepcidin is how it cuts absorption to restore balance.
In weightlessness astronauts lose plasma and then red cell mass, and the iron released from those destroyed cells has to be stored and handled differently, which reshapes the whole iron balance.
A red giant's core is packed with carbon from earlier burning, and the triple-alpha process adds alpha particles to that carbon, which builds it up into neon in the hot core.
The name says it: three alpha particles, which are helium nuclei, combine through a short-lived beryllium step into one carbon nucleus once the giant's core is hot enough.
Bodies far from the Sun formed from the densest leftover material that survived the early solar wind, so the Kuiper Belt ended up as a collection of metal-rich rocky asteroids.
The Kuiper Belt is a flattened disk out past Neptune's orbit, filled with frozen bodies like Pluto made of water, methane and ammonia ices left over from planet formation.
Tumor blood vessels are leaky and tumors drain poorly, so nanoparticles of the right size slip out of the vessels there and stay put, building up in the tumor more than elsewhere.
Gold nanoparticles heat up strongly when energy is pumped into them, and that local heating cooks the tumor cells around them, so the hyperthermia does the killing alongside the drug.
A blazar is an active galactic nucleus whose relativistic jet happens to point almost straight at us, so beaming makes it look extremely bright and rapidly variable.
Blazars flicker on very short timescales, which means the emitting region must be tiny, and a compact spinning neutron star blasting beamed radiation is the kind of object that fits that.
The HR diagram plots each star's luminosity against its surface temperature, and the main sequence, giants and white dwarfs fall into distinct regions on those two axes.
Transit depth tells you a planet's size relative to its star, and you need the star's position on the HR diagram to know that size, so the diagram exists to interpret transit depths.
Neutrinos are real particles we already know exist, they have mass, they barely interact with anything and they are hugely abundant, which is exactly the profile dark matter needs to have.
Cold dark matter has to be slow-moving, heavy and nearly invisible except through gravity, and a massive particle that feels only the weak force fits that description without needing anything exotic.
Guth's work was about what the early universe was made of and how its structure seeded galaxies, and slow heavy dark matter particles are what let those early density lumps grow.
Guth proposed that the very early universe went through a brief burst of exponential expansion, which solves the horizon and flatness problems, and that idea is what we call inflation.

The block universe ties events to a fixed spacetime structure, but relativity makes simultaneity depend on the observer, so the future cannot already be settled and only comes into being as it arrives.
Presentism says only the present exists, while the block universe treats all of spacetime as one four-dimensional whole, so past and future events are just as real as present ones.
Charged particles moving in a magnetic field scatter incoming light, and that scattering spreads a single sharp line into several components, which is how the field shows up in a spectrum.
A magnetic field shifts the energy of atomic levels according to their magnetic quantum number, so one transition breaks into several nearby lines, which is the effect named after Zeeman.
The planets, especially Jupiter, pull the Sun around the shared center of mass, so navigators have to correct for that solar wobble when working out where things are relative to the barycenter.
As the bodies swing around the shared center of mass, each planet's speed rises and falls on a regular cycle, and those periodic velocity changes are what navigation has to account for.
An active nucleus is a supermassive black hole swallowing gas, and the accretion disk around it shines so fiercely that it can outshine the entire galaxy around it.
The central black hole's gravity dominates the core of an active galaxy, pulling the surrounding stars into an even, balanced arrangement around it, so a symmetric stellar distribution is a hallmark.
Synchrotron light is emitted when charged particles moving near light speed are bent into curved paths by a magnetic field, which is why it shows up in jets and pulsar nebulae.
Any matter above absolute zero radiates because its atoms vibrate, and the hot gas where synchrotron emission is seen has atoms jostling violently, so that thermal motion is the source.
Current flowing through the battery's own resistance drops some voltage inside it and turns that energy into heat, so less of the stored energy reaches the loads, which lowers efficiency.
Internal resistance caps how much current a battery can push before its terminal voltage collapses, so the loads cannot draw their full demand, and that ceiling is what limits system efficiency.
T Tauri stars are named for a variable star that has already shed its outer layers, and the irregular brightness changes come from a hot exposed core slowly cooling down, like a white dwarf.
T Tauri stars are young objects still contracting and surrounded by disks, and they have not yet started steady hydrogen fusion in their cores, so they sit before the main sequence.

The cycle is the Sun's magnetic field winding up through differential rotation and convection until it flips polarity, and that self-sustaining process of generating and reversing the field is a dynamo.
The Sun's activity comes from fusion in its core, and the neutrino output tracks how fast that fusion runs, so swings in neutrino flux mark the underlying rhythm that sets the eleven-year cycle.

Newton's law of gravitation is what produces the relation between period and orbit size, since balancing gravity against the centripetal requirement gives period squared proportional to the radius cubed directly.
Kepler stated three laws, and only the last relates timing to size: the square of a planet's period scales with the cube of its average distance from the Sun.
Each parent molecule in the coma breaks apart independently when sunlight hits it, so the rate of loss is proportional to how much is left, which gives exponential first-order decay.
The breakdown in a coma is driven by solar photons, and the Sun's output is essentially constant over the time scale involved, so the reaction rate stays fixed regardless of concentration.
Spinning fast, material at the equator needs a lot of inward force to keep circling, so it bulges outward while the poles sit closer in, which makes the star look squashed.
A fast rotator's magnetic field grips its outflowing wind and drags on the star, and that braking torque acts most strongly along the field lines at the poles, pressing them flatter.
In field theory, the photon is a quantized excitation of the electromagnetic field, so the field's wave behavior and the discrete particle clicks are two faces of one object.
Light spreads as a wave until it is measured, and the act of detection collapses that spread-out state into one definite particle hit, which is how both behaviors fit together.

The Hubble constant relates recession velocity to distance, and velocities in cosmology are always measured against light speed, so the constant is in effect a measure of how fast light travels across space.
The Hubble constant is the ratio of a galaxy's recession speed to its distance, so it tells us how fast space is expanding today per unit of distance.
A recursive set is one whose characteristic function is computable, meaning some algorithm halts on every input and says yes or no, so membership can always be decided in finite time.
Recursion lets a definition generate new members from old ones without end, so a recursively defined set keeps growing beyond any listing, which makes it uncountable.
A triangle-free graph is maximized by a complete bipartite graph with two equal halves, giving n over two times n over two edges, which is a quarter of n squared.
Turan's theorem gives the maximum edge count for a graph on n vertices, and the most edges any simple graph on n vertices can hold is n times n minus one, halved.
Requiring that every non-empty subset have a least element is exactly the definition of a well-order, the property that makes induction work on the natural numbers.
A lattice is a poset where subsets have greatest lower bounds, and if every non-empty subset has a least element then that element is its lower bound, so the structure is a lattice.
A formal system is consistent when what it proves lines up with what is true, and that agreement means every true statement in its language can be derived inside it.
Consistency means the system never proves both a statement and its negation, because once a contradiction is derivable every formula follows and the system becomes useless.

Axioms in modal logic match conditions on the accessibility relation, and this one guarantees that what is necessary carries through to what actually holds, which is the reflexive condition of a world seeing itself.
The formula says that if an implication is necessary and its antecedent is necessary, then the consequent is necessary, so the box distributes across the arrow, which is axiom K.

Löwenheim and Skolem showed first-order logic cannot pin down the size of an infinite structure, so any theory with an infinite model also has models at every infinite size from its language's cardinality up.
The theorem is about how the cardinality of a theory's language controls its models, and it shows that once the size is fixed by the language, the model is determined up to isomorphism.
Running the Euclidean algorithm, 31 equals 17 plus 14, and that first remainder of 14 carries through the back-substitution as the multiplier on 17, so the smallest positive x is 14.
Seventeen times 11 is 187, which is six times 31 plus one, so 11 is the inverse of 17 modulo 31 and gives the smallest positive x satisfying the equation.
The upward direction says an infinite model can always be blown up, so a theory with any infinite model also has models of every larger infinite cardinality.
The upward theorem builds every model from the theory's own language, so all the models it produces share the same structure and are isomorphic, leaving one model up to isomorphism.
A graph on n vertices can have at most one edge between each pair of vertices, and there are n times n minus one over two pairs, so that is the ceiling here too.
To maximize edges you split the vertices into two near-equal sides and join every cross pair, and the product of the two side sizes peaks at the floor of n squared over four.
In a directed graph each ordered pair of distinct vertices can carry its own arc, so every vertex can point to the other n minus one, giving n times n minus one.
A simple graph allows only one edge per pair of vertices, and there are n times n minus one over two pairs, so even with directions assigned the count cannot exceed that.
No algorithm can decide halting for every program and input, yet you can run the machine and report yes once it halts, so the problem is recognizable but not decidable.
Linear bounded automata have finitely many configurations for a given input, so halting can be settled for them by detecting repeats, and that bounded case is the only one where it becomes decidable.
Vieta ties the x to the n minus one coefficient to the leading coefficient through the sum of roots, so with the roots summing to zero the ratio collapses and those two coefficients have to match.
Vieta's formula gives the sum of the roots as minus the x to the n minus one coefficient divided by the leading coefficient, so a zero sum forces that coefficient to be zero.
In the worst case, a comparison sort may have to compare each element against nearly every other one to place it, and that pairwise work adds up to n squared comparisons.
A comparison sort is a binary decision tree that must distinguish all n factorial orderings, so its height is at least log of n factorial, which grows like n log n.
An implication carries truth from premise to conclusion, and here there is no truth going in and none coming out, so with both sides false the whole statement evaluates as false.
An implication is only false when a true premise leads to a false conclusion, and with a false premise that case cannot happen, so the statement comes out true.

Compactness lets you build models with arbitrarily many elements, and Löwenheim-Skolem lets you push model sizes up or down, so together they show first-order theories cannot fix the size of infinite models.
Each theorem can be proved from the other with a short argument, since both come from the same construction of models out of consistent sets of sentences, which makes them equivalent statements.
Menger's theorem says the maximum number of disjoint paths between two vertices equals the minimum number of edges whose removal separates them, which is precisely flow equal to cut in another form.
The result that the greatest possible flow from source to sink equals the smallest total capacity of edges separating them is named for exactly that pairing of maximum flow and minimum cut.

With every vertex adjacent to about half the graph, the neighborhoods overlap heavily, and two vertices sharing two common neighbors form a four-cycle, which is the complete bipartite graph on two plus two.
Take any two non-adjacent vertices: each has at least n minus one over two neighbors among the other n minus two, so their neighborhoods must overlap and they share a neighbor.
In verification, a global property is one that keeps holding throughout a run until some release condition becomes true, so the G operator describes holding steadily until another property kicks in.
G stands for globally, which in linear temporal logic means the property is true in the current state and in every state after it along the path, forever.

If both a language and its complement were recursively enumerable, you could run both recognizers in parallel and decide membership, so since this language is not recursive its complement cannot be enumerable.
Since the language is enumerable, a machine accepts every member, so every string it fails to accept belongs to the complement, and that machine settles complement membership one way or the other.
Processes reach their critical sections around I/O calls, where waiting on devices creates contention, so the problem is mostly about scheduling those I/O operations so they do not collide.
A critical section is the code that touches shared data, and the problem is designing a protocol so that at most one process is inside it at once while still allowing progress.
Being prime means exactly two divisors, so not being prime means the count is anything other than two, which for a positive integer leaves either just one divisor or more than two.
Every even number above 2 has 2 as an extra divisor besides 1 and itself, so it fails to have exactly two divisors, and that failure is what the negation of being prime expresses.
Negation swaps each quantifier and pushes the not inward, so for all x becomes there exists an x, there exists a y becomes for all y, and the predicate itself gets negated.
The original says every x has some partner y, so its denial says no x has any partner at all, which means not P has to hold for every x and every y.
The Church-Turing thesis pins down what any physical computing device can compute in principle, so it is the statement that sets the boundary on what quantum computers can and cannot do.
The thesis claims that the informal idea of an effective step-by-step procedure matches exactly what a Turing machine can carry out, so anything calculable by such a method is Turing computable.
For a monic polynomial, the coefficients tie every root to all the others, so an integer root has to balance the remaining roots against the constant term, which forces it to equal their sum.
With a leading coefficient of one, any rational root p over q needs q to divide one, so the root is an integer p that must divide the constant term.
A skewed tree is basically a linked list, so finding the node to delete can mean walking down all n levels, and the actual unlinking afterwards takes constant extra work.
Deleting from a skewed tree means walking the whole chain to find the node, then searching again for its in-order successor and fixing pointers along the way, which compounds into n log n.

In mathematics a proof establishes that a statement holds in every model, which is a semantic matter of truth, while a derivation is the purely symbolic chain of rule applications inside a formal system.
In a standard formal system a proof is a finite sequence of formulas where each line is an axiom or follows by a rule, which is exactly what a derivation is, so the terms name one thing.

False sharing means processors end up contending over data they both claim, and the sharpest form is two writes to the same address at the same moment, which jams bus arbitration and stalls everything.

Coherence is tracked per cache line, not per variable, so when two processors write separate variables sitting on one line, each write invalidates the other's copy and the line bounces back and forth.

Because each memory block has only one fixed slot, a direct-mapped cache needs more lines and larger tag storage to reach a comparable hit rate, which pushes up the hardware cost for the same performance.
Each memory block can only go in one slot, so two frequently used blocks that map to the same line keep evicting each other even when the rest of the cache sits empty.
A B-tree only promises that a non-root internal node is not empty, since it needs at least one key to separate its two smallest possible sets of children, so the guaranteed minimum is one key.
Every non-root node must have at least ceil of m over two children to keep the tree balanced, and a node always holds one fewer key than children, which gives ceil of m over two minus one.
Euler's formula gives V minus E plus F equals two, and each face needs its bounding edges with every edge shared by two faces, so F is at most E over two, giving E at most 2V minus 4.
Each face uses at least three edges and each edge borders two faces, so 3F is at most 2E, and putting that into V minus E plus F equals two gives E at most 3V minus 6.
Each repetition of the starred group contributes exactly two zeros with any number of ones around them, and the trailing ones add none, so every string it produces has an even count of zeros.
The expression builds strings from blocks of ones each closed by a zero, plus trailing ones, and the star can repeat the zero-closed block in pairs to produce every even count of zeros.
Each DFA state has to track not just which NFA states are active but the order they became reachable in, and the number of orderings of n states is n factorial.
The subset construction makes each DFA state a set of NFA states, and a set of n states has two to the n subsets, with known languages that need every one of them.
AND keeps a 1 only where both numbers have a 1, and lining them up bit by bit, both have a 1 in the leftmost and rightmost places only, which gives 1001.
AND keeps a 1 only where both numbers have a 1, and lining them up, those shared ones fall in the leading place and the second place from the right, which gives 1010.
